text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text data, such as books, websites, and articles. To get good results, users often practise prompt engineering, which means writing clear instructions. LLMs can help with tasks like writing, translating, and answering questions. However, they also have limits. They sometimes make mistakes, cannot truly understand meaning, and may reflect biases found in their training data. So, while LLMs are powerful tools, it is important to check their answers carefully.
